title: Dropping new ideas here weekly, focusing on finding the fun. Week 5: Bankroll
author: StaticAnchor
selftext:
Hey everyone!

Another week, another game idea.

I actually did things different this week.

Bankroll was an idea I had for a while that I've been sitting on. I had a really fun thought about rolling dice around on a board and lighting it up, and collecting coins in the process. I put it together and shared it with some family, who seemed to really like it.

I got happy ears, and went nuts on the game.

I built all of these interesting mechanics and systems, ways to upgrade and progress. By the end of the week, it looked like one big sloppy mess and I felt a ton of anxiety around it.

AI driven workflows have been a blessing and curse for someone like me. Who's mind runs a mile a minute and has access to a tool that won't tell you "no".

This past week, I actually really slowed down and got intentional about it. I took the core loop of the game, and just focused on polish. I've been so quick to release my ideas, that I'm building out all of these power ups and secrets and progression that I feel like don't showcase the fun well.

Well this week, it was all about polish. I had a blast making it. I focused on finding different aesthetics and inspiration from design, and build a complete tool around designing how a game looks and feels, and being able to save multiple ideas of how the game could look.

Sometimes I struggle on the vision. I know how the game should feel, but not quite sure what it should actually visually look like. Now I have a tool that helps me visualize it, tweak it, and get it right.

The tool is called Juicebox, and I'll be showcasing that early next week along with some of the other aesthetic presets, and sharing it with the community to try out and possibly polish your own games.

Until then, enjoy Bankroll, a simple game about rolling dice around and earning some coins. How high can you go?

[Bankroll Demo](https://hookandloopgames.itch.io/bankroll)
